module_title: Human Physiology I: Anatomy of Digestion, Breathing & Circulation
introduction: This foundational level establishes the structural blueprints of three vital systems: the Digestive system (fuel intake), the Respiratory system (gas exchange), and the Circulatory system (internal transport). Mastery of anatomical landmarks and basic fluid compositions is crucial.

core_concepts.title: Digestive System Anatomy & Dentition
core_concepts.description:
1. Dentition: Human teeth are Thecodont (embedded in jaw sockets), Diphyodont (two sets during life: deciduous/milk teeth and permanent teeth), and Heterodont (four types: Incisors, Canines, Premolars, Molars). The dental formula of an adult human is 2123/2123. 
2. Alimentary Canal: 
- Pharynx: Common passage for food and air. The Epiglottis (cartilaginous flap) prevents food from entering the glottis.
- Stomach: J-shaped bag with 4 parts: Cardiac, Fundic, Body, and Pyloric. 
- Small Intestine (SI): Duodenum (C-shaped), Jejunum (coiled), Ileum (highly coiled).
- Large Intestine (LI): Caecum (hosts symbiotic microbes, bears vermiform appendix), Colon (Ascending, Transverse, Descending, Sigmoid), Rectum.

core_concepts.title: Digestive Glands
core_concepts.description:
1. Salivary Glands: Three pairs (Parotid - cheek, Sub-maxillary/Sub-mandibular - lower jaw, Sub-lingual - below tongue).
2. Liver: Largest gland (1.2 - 1.5 kg). Consists of hepatic lobules (structural and functional units). Secretes bile, which is stored and concentrated in the Gall Bladder. 
3. Pancreas: Heterocrine (both exocrine and endocrine) gland. Exocrine portion secretes an alkaline pancreatic juice; endocrine portion (Islets of Langerhans) secretes hormones (insulin, glucagon).

core_concepts.title: Respiratory System Anatomy
core_concepts.description:
Pathway of air: External Nostrils $\rightarrow$ Nasal passage $\rightarrow$ Nasal cavity $\rightarrow$ Pharynx $\rightarrow$ Larynx (Sound box, made of cartilage) $\rightarrow$ Trachea $\rightarrow$ Primary Bronchi $\rightarrow$ Secondary/Tertiary Bronchi $\rightarrow$ Bronchioles $\rightarrow$ Alveoli (thin, vascularized bags for gas exchange). 
The Trachea, primary, secondary, and tertiary bronchi, and initial bronchioles are supported by INCOMPLETE cartilaginous rings (C-shaped, open dorsally). The lungs are covered by a double-layered Pleura with pleural fluid between them to reduce friction.

core_concepts.title: Blood and Heart Anatomy
core_concepts.description:
1. Blood Composition: Fluid connective tissue. Plasma (55%, contains fibrinogen, globulins, albumins) and Formed Elements (45% - Erythrocytes/RBCs, Leucocytes/WBCs, Platelets/Thrombocytes). 
2. Heart Anatomy: Mesodermally derived. Four chambers (2 Atria, 2 Ventricles). Separated by Interatrial septum, Interventricular septum, and Atrio-ventricular septa.
3. Valves: Tricuspid valve (between Right Atrium & Right Ventricle), Bicuspid/Mitral valve (between Left Atrium & Left Ventricle), Semilunar valves (at the openings of Pulmonary artery and Aorta). Valves prevent the backflow of blood.

important_entities.name: Sphincter of Oddi
important_entities.key_fact: Guards the opening of the hepato-pancreatic duct into the duodenum.
important_entities.significance: The bile duct and the pancreatic duct join together to form the common hepato-pancreatic duct. The Sphincter of Oddi controls the release of both bile (for fat emulsification) and pancreatic juice (digestive enzymes) into the small intestine exactly when food enters the duodenum.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Students often memorize 'Arteries carry oxygenated blood, Veins carry deoxygenated blood.' This is a massive trap. The strictly correct definition is: Arteries carry blood AWAY from the heart, Veins carry blood TOWARDS the heart. EXCEPTION: The Pulmonary Artery carries DEOXYGENATED blood to the lungs, and the Pulmonary Veins carry OXYGENATED blood back to the left atrium.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation:
Decreasing order of Leucocyte abundance in human blood: 
**N**eutrophils (60-65%)
**L**ymphocytes (20-25%)
**M**onocytes (6-8%)
**E**osinophils (2-3%)
**B**asophils (0.5-1%)

exam_strategy_tips: Always remember the specific cells of the gastric glands: Mucous neck cells (secrete mucus), Peptic/Chief cells (secrete proenzyme pepsinogen), and Parietal/Oxyntic cells (secrete HCl and Intrinsic factor essential for Vitamin B12 absorption).
